knownExtent.basis: The New Italy Museum holding is a heterogeneous, changing collection of settler photographs and documents with no stable finite public-domain boundary; the identified public-domain acquisition candidates are named in the suspected[] leads, but the campaign's extent itself is unbounded.

entries.description: The official French court decisions in the de Rays fraud prosecution: the first-instance jugement (tribunal correctionnel de la Seine, 8e chambre, 1884) and the Cour de Paris appeal arret (Chambre des appels de police correctionnelle, 14 May 1884), plus the Cour de cassation decision confirming conviction.
entries.basis: Distinct from the published PLEADINGS the bundle already holds/knows (PB-P008 Las Cases pleading; PB-P012 Vermont plaidoiries): these are the courts' own decisions. The chronology (Seine 1884 conviction -> Paris appeal rejected 14 May 1884 -> cassation) is attested in the secondary literature and press. Such decisions are recorded in the contemporary legal serials -- Gazette des Tribunaux, Gazette du Palais (jurisprudence et legislation), Recueil Dalloz, and the Bulletin des arrets de la Cour de cassation rendus en matiere criminelle (all digitized on Gallica) -- rather than as standalone monographs; locating the specific de Rays issues/entries within those serial runs is the open inventory step (SRCH-0002/SRCH-0004). Serial home confirmed: the Gazette des Tribunaux (Paris) is digitized on Gallica (ark cb34447990d, date-browsable); the appeal arret (14 May 1884) should sit in the ~15-16 May 1884 issue -- pinpointing the exact issue/folios is a shipped-fetcher/IIIF date-browse step.

entries.basis: Australian photograph, creation year 1890 (grounded from the object description). The pre-1969 photograph copyright term has expired (not revived by the 2005 extension), so it is public domain once digitized with provenance. Per PB-P006 settlement-photograph research.

entries.description: School Group Photo New Italy 1903 (New Italy Museum, accession NIMI-0845) — a pre-1955 settlement photograph
entries.basis: Australian photograph, creation year 1903 (grounded from the object description). The pre-1969 photograph term has expired — the correct public-domain rights profile. Per PB-P006 settlement-photograph research.

resolution.reason: Source master-image link is broken on the museum's Musarch page (image_anchor href truncated to './images/000845_', no filename/extension) — no retrievable full-res master to acquire.

entries.description: Landing site of settlement at Port Breton (New Italy Museum, accession NIMI-0668)
entries.basis: Named as a settlement-history photograph candidate in earlier research; on live per-item inventory it proved to be an HTML-only catalogue record with no digital image.

resolution.reason: HTML-only catalogue record: no image_anchor (no downloadable master) and no creation date on the page (blank Object Date, no year in the description) — nothing to acquire and no basis to date.

entries.description: 'Survivors arrival in Sydney 1881' — an artists impression of the Italian immigrants (New Italy Museum, accession NIMI-0855)
entries.basis: Previously listed among the settlement-photograph candidates, but live per-item inventory shows it is an ARTIST'S IMPRESSION (an artwork), not a photograph. PB-P006's public-domain basis covers pre-1955 photographs, which does not apply to an artwork whose author and creation date are unestablished.

resolution.reason: An artist's impression (artwork), not a photograph; the pre-1955-photograph public-domain basis does not apply, and the artwork's author/creation date are unestablished. Operator decision: do not acquire.

entries.description: 'Expedition Survivors Group Photo 1961' (New Italy Museum) — a post-1955 settlement photograph
entries.basis: A settlement photograph, but created 1961 — after the pre-1955 threshold, so still within the Australian photograph copyright term. Excluded from the public-domain acquisition set.

resolution.reason: Created 1961 — post-1955, still in copyright under the Australian photograph term; not public domain.

entries.description: Survivor accounts, letters, and personal writings of the de Rays expedition settlers
entries.basis: The museum's Documents category holds settler writings; a first-hand written account of the voyage/colony/collapse would be Port-Breton-CENTRAL primary source, unlike the settlement photographs. Rights are the literary-work regime (author's life + 70y), not the photograph term.

resolution.reason: The Documents category was examined via the shipped museum path: the potentially-central primary writings (diaries/letters/journals/passport/map) are physical-only -- NOT digitised, no image master to acquire. The digitised documents are corpus-adjacent settlement certificates + book artifacts, no first-hand Port Breton account. A physical-only residual; acquirable only out-of-band, not through the pipeline.
